mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the periods with sustained GDP growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in industrial production by more than 1% in a month indicates supply chain disruptions or reduced economic activity, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are negatively impacted.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls by more than 300,000 in a month, combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate, signals a strong labor market and economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 300,000 in 1 month and UNRATE decreases
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in housing starts by more than 10% in a month indicates a weakening demand in the housing market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the consumer price index (CPI) over two consecutive months signals inflationary pressures, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the Federal Reserve is likely to tighten monetary policy.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the periods with sustained CPI increases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in retail and food services sales by more than 1% in a month, combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate, signals strong consumer demand and economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are positively impacted.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 1% in 1 month and UNRATE decreases
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.
